DRAGON / CONTRIBUTOR ACCESS

Before you
enter the room.

DragonsRitual gives invited contributors access to private creative spaces, unpublished work, editorial tools, and developing projects. This agreement keeps that material inside the studio while protecting the contributor's own work.

THE SHORT VERSION
  • Private and unpublished material stays inside DragonsRitual.
  • Do not screenshot, copy, leak, repost, or discuss confidential studio material outside the project.
  • Your original work remains yours unless a separate written agreement says otherwise.
  • Submitting work gives DragonsRitual permission to review it; publication requires editorial approval.
  • If DragonsRitual publishes your accepted work, you grant the studio the license described below to display and promote it.
  • Only upload material you created or have permission to use.
  • Contributor access can be ended by either side.
  • Confidentiality continues after access ends.
DRAGONSRITUAL CONTRIBUTOR AGREEMENTVERSION 1.0 · AUGUST 2026

1. Purpose and contributor access

This Contributor Agreement ("Agreement") governs access to private contributor areas, editorial systems, unpublished materials, and collaborative spaces operated under the DragonsRitual name ("DragonsRitual"). Access is provided so the contributor can create, submit, discuss, and develop original creative work for possible publication, collaboration, promotion, or other mutually agreed projects.

Contributor access is personal. The contributor will not share login credentials, private links, access tokens, passwords, unpublished files, or other methods of entering restricted DragonsRitual systems with another person.

2. Confidential and inside information

"Confidential Information" means non-public information the contributor learns, receives, views, or accesses through DragonsRitual, including unpublished writing, artwork, music, videos, game builds, source code, designs, concepts, project plans, business plans, launch plans, editorial discussions, contributor information, private messages intended for the project, internal documents, private links, credentials, technical information, and other material that is clearly private, internal, unreleased, draft, confidential, or contributor-only.

The contributor will keep Confidential Information inside DragonsRitual and will not, without permission, disclose it to outsiders; post or transmit it publicly; reproduce it for unrelated use; photograph or screenshot it for distribution; publish excerpts; or use it to compete with, impersonate, exploit, or harm DragonsRitual or another contributor.

These restrictions do not apply to information that becomes publicly released by DragonsRitual or the rightful owner, was lawfully known to the contributor before access, is independently developed without using Confidential Information, or must be disclosed by law. If legally permitted, the contributor should give DragonsRitual reasonable notice before a legally compelled disclosure.

3. Contributor ownership

The contributor keeps ownership of original work the contributor created before joining DragonsRitual and of new original work the contributor creates, unless the contributor and DragonsRitual later sign a separate written agreement that expressly transfers ownership. Access to the Writer Room does not by itself transfer copyright ownership to DragonsRitual.

Draft storage and personal backups

The Writer Room may provide draft-saving and autosave features as a convenience, but it is not intended to be the contributor's only archive or backup system. The contributor is responsible for keeping an independent copy of important drafts, source files, notes, and other creative work. DragonsRitual cannot guarantee that every draft, revision, upload, or locally cached change will always be recoverable after a device, browser, network, account, software, hosting, or service failure.

4. Submission, editorial review, and publication license

Submitting material to the DragonsRitual editorial system is a request for review, not automatic publication. DragonsRitual may accept, decline, return, request revisions, edit by mutual coordination, choose placement, schedule, feature, archive, or remove submitted material. The contributor should raise any requested credit, context, or restrictions with the editor before publication.

When the contributor knowingly approves a work for publication by DragonsRitual, the contributor grants DragonsRitual a non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free license to publish, reproduce, display, distribute, format, excerpt for promotional purposes, link to, archive, and promote that accepted work through DragonsRitual websites, social channels, newsletters, promotional materials, and related studio channels. Because the license is non-exclusive, the contributor may continue using and publishing the contributor's work elsewhere unless a separate written agreement says otherwise.

DragonsRitual will make reasonable efforts to preserve the contributor's agreed credit/byline. Material may be reformatted for layout, accessibility, technical compatibility, excerpts, previews, thumbnails, or promotion without changing the fundamental authorship of the work.

5. Rights to uploaded material

The contributor will submit only material the contributor owns or has permission to use. The contributor will not knowingly submit plagiarized writing, unauthorized copyrighted images, music, video, private personal information, malware, or material that the contributor has no right to provide. If third-party material requires attribution or a specific license, the contributor will identify that requirement to the editor.

6. Compensation, employment, and future projects

Creating a contributor account and receiving access does not by itself create employment, a partnership, an agency relationship, or a promise of payment. Any compensation, commission, revenue share, work-for-hire arrangement, ownership transfer, deadline, exclusivity term, or paid assignment must be separately agreed in writing before it applies.

The parties may later choose to collaborate on games, publications, art, music, events, or other projects. Those projects may require additional project-specific terms.

7. Community and professional conduct

Contributor access is intended for good-faith creative collaboration. The contributor will not use private systems to harass other contributors, intentionally damage the service, obtain unauthorized access, impersonate another user, scrape private material, or interfere with the work of others. Editorial disagreement alone is not a violation of this Agreement.

8. Ending access

Either the contributor or DragonsRitual may end the contributor relationship. DragonsRitual may suspend or remove private access when reasonably necessary to protect the studio, contributors, systems, or confidential work. Ending access does not erase rights already granted for work that was previously published unless DragonsRitual and the contributor agree otherwise in writing.

9. Continuing confidentiality

The obligations concerning Confidential Information continue after contributor access ends for as long as the information remains non-public and confidential. Trade secrets, if any, remain protected for as long as they legally qualify as trade secrets.

10. Entire contributor-access understanding

This Agreement applies to contributor access and does not replace a later written agreement covering a specific paid assignment, ownership transfer, work-for-hire project, licensing deal, or other specialized collaboration. If a later signed agreement directly conflicts with this Agreement for a specific project, the project-specific agreement controls for that project.

This contributor-access agreement is intended as a practical working agreement and is not a substitute for advice from an attorney. DragonsRitual may ask contributors to accept an updated version if the contributor program materially changes.
